title: Apple's new chief executive says the company does not want to ship AI for its own sake
friendlyTitle: Apple's new chief executive says the company does not want to ship AI just to say it did
summary: On 31 October, TechCrunch reported a Wired interview with John Ternus, who became Apple's chief executive at the start of September. Ternus said Apple will use AI in new products, and that the company does not want to ship AI for AI's sake. His test, as quoted, is that people should not have to ask whether AI or ordinary software did the work. Asked whether agents could make apps unnecessary, he said that could make life easy, and that making products is still a human job.
friendlySummary: On 31 October, TechCrunch reported a Wired interview with John Ternus, who became Apple's chief executive at the start of September. Ternus said Apple will use AI in new products, and that the company does not want to ship AI just to have AI. His test, as quoted, is that people should not have to ask whether AI or ordinary software did the work. Asked whether agents could make apps unnecessary, he said that could make life easy, and that making products is still a human job.
whyItMatters: This does not add a feature you can turn on today, and it does not move the newer Siri. It is the stated test for the products that do ship: whether you would keep the result if nobody told you a model was involved. If you are waiting on Apple Intelligence, that is the bar Ternus is describing, not a date.
